      "title": "Crash when Google Meet location is used without destination calendars",
      "body": "In `EventManager.create`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array. The condition immediately accesses `.integration` on it, which throws a TypeError. This breaks booking creation for Google Meet events when no destination calendar is set. Use optional chaining or a safe default before comparing integration."

    {

      "category": "bug",
      "title": "updateEvent can be called with an undefined credential",
      "body": "In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, when a booking reference has `credentialId` but the credential is not present in memory and cannot be loaded from the database, `credential` remains undefined. The code still pushes `updateEvent(credential, ...)`, which will crash in `CalendarManager.updateEvent` when it reads credential properties or calls `getCalendar`. Add a guard and emit a failed result instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
      "line": 399,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Duplicate event creation possible for other_calendar integrations",
      "body": "`createAllCalendarEvents` processes destination calendars and then unconditionally creates events for every credential whose type includes `other_calendar`. If a destination calendar entry already points to an `other_calendar` credential, the same event is created twice, causing duplicate CRM/non-traditional calendar entries. Deduplicate by credential or type."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
      "line": 554,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Only the first old calendar event is deleted when merging bookings",
      "body": "When `newBookingId` is provided, `updateAllCalendarEvents` finds only the first old calendar reference from the original booking and deletes it. For collective bookings with multiple host calendar references, the remaining old calendar events are not deleted, leaving stale external calendar entries. Delete all relevant old calendar references."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts",
      "line": 1078,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Collective host destination calendars are discarded when main calendar is absent",
      "body": "The collective booking path initializes `evt.destinationCalendar` to null when neither event type nor organizer has a destination calendar, then uses `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If it is null, the push is skipped and all team-member destination calendars are lost, so their calendar events will not be created. Initialize the array before pushing."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 256,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Google updateEvent fallback cannot select a calendar when externalCalendarId is missing",
      "body": "In `updateEvent`, if `externalCalendarId` is falsy the fallback searches `event.destinationCalendar` for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, i.e. for undefined/empty. This returns no calendar, so the Google API update may be called with an undefined `calendarId` and fail. It should fall back to the first/primary destination calendar."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 317,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Google deleteEvent may target primary calendar when actual destination is unknown",
      "body": "In `deleteEvent`, when `externalCalendarId` is missing the fallback again searches for `externalId === externalCalendarId` and yields undefined. The code then falls back to `primary`. If the event was created on a non-primary calendar, deletion will 404 and resolve without deleting the actual event, leaving stale calendar entries."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 168,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Google hangout-link patch can use undefined calendarId",
      "body": "`createEvent` inserts the event with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || 'primary'`, but the follow-up `events.patch` uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. If no selected calendar was found, the event is created on primary but the patch is sent with undefined calendarId, so updating the description with the hangout link can fail. Use the same fallback for the patch."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 129,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar",
      "body": "`LarkCalendarService.createEvent` ignores the credential being used and always takes the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar`. For collective events with multiple destination calendars, this can use a calendar belonging to another provider/host or fail when the first entry is not a Lark calendar. It should select the destination calendar matching the credential/integration."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 75,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Office 365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar",
      "body": "`Office365CalendarService.createEvent` builds the Graph URL from the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar`. When multiple hosts have different calendars, this can target a non-Office external ID or the wrong host calendar, causing event creation to fail. It should choose the destination calendar associated with the credential being used."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 162,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "CalDAV createEvent can silently skip event creation for secondary hosts",
      "body": "`BaseCalendarService.createEvent` filters calendars by the first destination calendar's `externalId`. If this service is invoked for a secondary host or the first destination is not in this CalDAV account, the filtered calendar list is empty and the method returns success without creating any event. This silently drops calendar events."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts",
      "line": 454,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Recurring cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference per booking",
      "body": "For recurring cancellations, the code loops over all user calendar credentials and, for each updated booking, deletes only the first calendar reference it finds. With multiple host calendar references this leaves other hosts' events undeleted and also attempts deletes with credentials that may not own the reference. It should iterate all matching booking references and use their credential IDs."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts",
      "line": 619,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "`await apiDeletes` does not await deletion promises",
      "body": "In the paid cancellation branch, `apiDeletes` is an array of promises, but `await apiDeletes` awaits the array itself rather than its promises. The handler can return success before calendar deletions finish and will not catch their failures. Use `await Promise.allSettled(apiDeletes)` or equivalent."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts",
      "line": 151,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Organization slug condition is inverted",
      "body": "The slug spread was changed from including `slug` when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false to including it when true. This reverses the previous behavior: organizations get a slug in billing-enabled environments and no slug when billing is disabled, which can break organization creation/billing flows."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/types/Calendar.d.ts",
      "line": 171,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Breaking/inconsistent destinationCalendar payload change",
      "body": "Changing `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object/null to an array changes webhook/API payload shape. Handlers are also inconsistent: some emit `[]` while others can emit `null`. External consumers expecting the previous shape may break; this should be normalized or documented as a breaking change."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts",

      "severity": "low",

      "title": "Webhook tests do not consistently cover new destinationCalendar shape",
      "body": "The test now expects `destinationCalendar: []` for BOOKING_REJECTED but still expects `null` for BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED. This inconsistency indicates the payload shape after the array change is not uniformly covered, and there are no automated tests for the collective multiple-host calendar behavior introduced by this PR."
    }

findings.title: Crash when Google Meet location is used without destination calendars
findings.body: In `EventManager.create`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array. The condition immediately accesses `.integration` on it, which throws a TypeError. This breaks booking creation for Google Meet events when no destination calendar is set. Use optional chaining or a safe default before comparing integration.

findings.title: updateEvent can be called with an undefined credential
findings.body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, when a booking reference has `credentialId` but the credential is not present in memory and cannot be loaded from the database, `credential` remains undefined. The code still pushes `updateEvent(credential, ...)`, which will crash in `CalendarManager.updateEvent` when it reads credential properties or calls `getCalendar`. Add a guard and emit a failed result instead.

findings.title: Duplicate event creation possible for other_calendar integrations
findings.body: `createAllCalendarEvents` processes destination calendars and then unconditionally creates events for every credential whose type includes `other_calendar`. If a destination calendar entry already points to an `other_calendar` credential, the same event is created twice, causing duplicate CRM/non-traditional calendar entries. Deduplicate by credential or type.

findings.title: Only the first old calendar event is deleted when merging bookings
findings.body: When `newBookingId` is provided, `updateAllCalendarEvents` finds only the first old calendar reference from the original booking and deletes it. For collective bookings with multiple host calendar references, the remaining old calendar events are not deleted, leaving stale external calendar entries. Delete all relevant old calendar references.

findings.title: Collective host destination calendars are discarded when main calendar is absent
findings.body: The collective booking path initializes `evt.destinationCalendar` to null when neither event type nor organizer has a destination calendar, then uses `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If it is null, the push is skipped and all team-member destination calendars are lost, so their calendar events will not be created. Initialize the array before pushing.

findings.title: Google updateEvent fallback cannot select a calendar when externalCalendarId is missing
findings.body: In `updateEvent`, if `externalCalendarId` is falsy the fallback searches `event.destinationCalendar` for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, i.e. for undefined/empty. This returns no calendar, so the Google API update may be called with an undefined `calendarId` and fail. It should fall back to the first/primary destination calendar.

findings.title: Google deleteEvent may target primary calendar when actual destination is unknown
findings.body: In `deleteEvent`, when `externalCalendarId` is missing the fallback again searches for `externalId === externalCalendarId` and yields undefined. The code then falls back to `primary`. If the event was created on a non-primary calendar, deletion will 404 and resolve without deleting the actual event, leaving stale calendar entries.

findings.title: Google hangout-link patch can use undefined calendarId
findings.body: `createEvent` inserts the event with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || 'primary'`, but the follow-up `events.patch` uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. If no selected calendar was found, the event is created on primary but the patch is sent with undefined calendarId, so updating the description with the hangout link can fail. Use the same fallback for the patch.

findings.title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
findings.body: `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` ignores the credential being used and always takes the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar`. For collective events with multiple destination calendars, this can use a calendar belonging to another provider/host or fail when the first entry is not a Lark calendar. It should select the destination calendar matching the credential/integration.

findings.title: Office 365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
findings.body: `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` builds the Graph URL from the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar`. When multiple hosts have different calendars, this can target a non-Office external ID or the wrong host calendar, causing event creation to fail. It should choose the destination calendar associated with the credential being used.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent can silently skip event creation for secondary hosts
findings.body: `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` filters calendars by the first destination calendar's `externalId`. If this service is invoked for a secondary host or the first destination is not in this CalDAV account, the filtered calendar list is empty and the method returns success without creating any event. This silently drops calendar events.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference per booking
findings.body: For recurring cancellations, the code loops over all user calendar credentials and, for each updated booking, deletes only the first calendar reference it finds. With multiple host calendar references this leaves other hosts' events undeleted and also attempts deletes with credentials that may not own the reference. It should iterate all matching booking references and use their credential IDs.

findings.title: `await apiDeletes` does not await deletion promises
findings.body: In the paid cancellation branch, `apiDeletes` is an array of promises, but `await apiDeletes` awaits the array itself rather than its promises. The handler can return success before calendar deletions finish and will not catch their failures. Use `await Promise.allSettled(apiDeletes)` or equivalent.

findings.title: Organization slug condition is inverted
findings.body: The slug spread was changed from including `slug` when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false to including it when true. This reverses the previous behavior: organizations get a slug in billing-enabled environments and no slug when billing is disabled, which can break organization creation/billing flows.

findings.title: Breaking/inconsistent destinationCalendar payload change
findings.body: Changing `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object/null to an array changes webhook/API payload shape. Handlers are also inconsistent: some emit `[]` while others can emit `null`. External consumers expecting the previous shape may break; this should be normalized or documented as a breaking change.

findings.title: Webhook tests do not consistently cover new destinationCalendar shape
findings.body: The test now expects `destinationCalendar: []` for BOOKING_REJECTED but still expects `null` for BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED. This inconsistency indicates the payload shape after the array change is not uniformly covered, and there are no automated tests for the collective multiple-host calendar behavior introduced by this PR.
